qt: to the Commission Esther Herranz García (PPE) Subject:

The implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation is making it difficult to secure a supply of soybean meal that complies with the traceability requirements laid down by the European Union. Brazil is the main supplier to Europe, accounting for 51.1 % of imports of soybeans and soybean meal. However, according to industry estimates, only around 70 % of the Brazilian soybean meal available is said to be compliant. This situation, combined with storage and transport constraints and differences between production regions, could lead to a shortfall of up to 4 million tonnes for the following marketing year. In light of the above: 1.
What measures does the Commission intend to take to avoid potential problems with the supply of soybean meal on the European market as a result of the implementation of the Deforestation Regulation?

What support tools does the Commission intend to implement to make it easier for producers and operators to comply with the traceability requirements of the Regulation, thereby avoiding problems with the supply of soybean meal in the EU?
Does the Commission intend to draw up a delegated act amending Annex I to exclude soyabean cake and meal intended for animal feed, as it has done for other products?
